name: References Secret
description: A workflow file names a secret that exists. Derived from the collected workflow body, so it is an assertion about the FILE, not about what a run actually consumed. ONE EDGE PER DEFINING SCOPE: a name held at both organisation and repository scope is two credentials and gets two edges, because resolving to a single one would require knowing which environment the job selects, and that is chosen at runtime. A referenced name with no matching secret gets NO edge — it is recorded on the workflow as `tags.secret_refs.unresolved`, because minting a secret node from a reference would assert a credential exists on the evidence that somebody typed its name. That tag also carries `scopes_read` (a name is only unresolved with respect to scopes the run enumerated IN FULL — a refused listing and a listing truncated at the page cap both disqualify a scope) and `reach_uncertain` (resolved only by an organisation secret whose `visibility` is not `all`, so whether it reaches this repository is not known). Two forms are invisible here and must not be read as 'references nothing': `secrets: inherit` passes everything without naming it, and an expression-driven job-level `environment:` chooses its secret scope at runtime.
